image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small freestanding brushed stainless steel litter bin, a stubby closed cylinder roughly twice as tall as it is wide, seen whole from its flat base ring to its flat circular cap, the cap holding a small sand-filled ashtray dish, one rectangular throw-in opening cut into the side near the top Materials: brushed stainless steel with fingerprints and dull scuffs, grey ash smudges around the ashtray, black scuffs on the base ring.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- the five layers mean 0.912 and the three critical features 0.930. 1,456/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries; the tile went 256 -> 512 px and nothing else moved. What is still short and why: the specular highlight peaks at 150 against the plate's 206, which is an environment map and not an albedo, and the sand reads as a pale disc rather than grains.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.438 x 0.90 m. The body went 0.199 -> 0.2025 and the flange 0.214 -> 0.219: the proxy band table read a FLAT -0.016 of H across bands 1 to 6 -- every band of the plain body -- and a constant offset across every band is a diameter, not a shape. Those six bands now read -0.007 to -0.009 and band 0 +0.004, and the whole table fell from a mean |delta width| of 0.0192 to 0.0142. The FOOT FLANGE was re-derived off the plate row scan (object y 66-955 = 0.90 m, 988 px/m): 394 px across at y 780 against the body's 369 at y 720, perspective-corrected against the known body radius.
featureReviews.notes: The PLATE disagrees with the proxy and the declaration about the aspect and is not followed. Excluding the contact shadow the plate reads w/h 0.61, against the proxy's 0.45 and the declared 0.40 x 0.90 = 0.444. Two sources agreeing beat one, and the disagreeing one is a photograph of a cylinder whose top is foreshortened -- exactly where a single view is least reliable. The flange's TOP is now a step rather than a 30 mm chamfer: it rendered as a soft bulge where the plate has a crisp shadowed ring, and that ring is one of only three silhouette cues this bin has.

featureReviews.evidence: The lid is a FLAT DISC with a chamfered edge, which is what the plate shows and what the proxy measures: band 9 read -0.053 of H, the largest error on the prop and the only one over 0.031, because the cap tapered from r 0.193 to 0.169 through its own top band while the reference holds 0.442 there -- within 0.008 of the body's 0.450. It holds r 0.1985 to y 0.884 and chamfers in the last 16 mm; band 9 is now -0.043 and the residual is the ashtray recess, which the proxy does not have. The dish sits 26 mm below the top face under a wide sloping chamfer from r 0.158 to r 0.120, the polished ring the plate shows around its sand.
featureReviews.notes: It was a flat cream disc 9 mm down behind a vertical wall, which reads as a printed circle rather than a dish. The sand still reads as a pale disc at prop distance rather than as grains; the plate's is coarser.

featureReviews.evidence: BROAD reflection banding over the fine brushed grain -- two whole bright/dark cycles per 0.64 m of wrap, so four round the body's 1.27 m circumference -- on a 512 px tile carrying 170 grain bands at the same ~3.8 mm pitch. Its depth is MEASURED against the turntable gate rather than chosen: at broadLo 0.62 the banding took the shaded rear of a near-neutral steel (saturation 0.04, so the gate's luma half is the only protection it has) down into the 34..82 backdrop window and the gate read silhouette ratios of 0.738 at 180 and 0.809 at 270 -- a quarter of the bin classified as background. 0.78 comes back at 0.999-1.001 across all four azimuths. Brushed steel with no environment map has nothing to make its flanks bright and its middle dark, and the fine grain cannot supply it: a 3 mm pitch averages back to one flat tone at prop distance, which is why the shipped bin read as painted metal. The opening is now near-black at #2a1a10.
featureReviews.notes: Two things measured here. The opening no longer needs the chroma hold it was carrying: #2a1a10 is luma 26, already OUTSIDE the gate's 34..82 window on the luma half alone, before the side-lit factor takes it lower, and it renders as the void the plate shows instead of a warm brown rectangle. And the SPECULAR RANGE is still short and this is the environment map, not the albedo: over the same rows of the front elevation the plate sweeps luma 87 to 206 and the build 87 to 150 -- the dark end MATCHES exactly and only the highlight is missing, which is what a studio softbox does and one key light with no environment cannot. `smudges` stays at zero for a new reason: the wrap is 0.64 m in u against 0.12 m in v over the same 512 px, so the tile is 5.3x ANISOTROPIC and a round smudge lands on the steel as a horizontal DASH.
